shadows.name: ground-halo-pine

shadows.name: ground-halo-slate

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: All movement: button rise, row slide.

motion.name: row-slide
motion.purpose: Row name and arrow circle slide.

motion.name: mower
motion.value: auto 120px/s; follow eased x7, capped 700px/s; resume after 4s idle; cut to 0.24 height; regrow 0.09/s

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition-duration .01ms; Field draws one still frame

field.renderer: Field(canvas, options) inside the living-field IIFE in index.html

options.grass: [{h:[min,max], w, c:[colors]}] back to front; last layer = next band's color
options.drift: {h:[back,front], amp, c:[back, front]}; front = next band's color
options.base: 3px seam strip in the next band's color
options.mower: true adds Dev's push mower to a grass field (hero only): mows alone until touched, then follows pointer/finger; grass regrows, clippings fly

instances: hero: 4 grass layers to sage + resting leaves + mower
edge sage-slate: snowbank-crest drift to slate
winter: snowfall + drift to snow white
edge snow-pine: spring grass to pine
field.mowZone: .mow-zone over the hero lawn band (96px, 120px from 561px), touch-action:none; html overscroll-behavior-y:none

narrative.overview:
The page is Dev's workplace, not a contractor's brochure: the yards and driveways of Ocean County, walked top to bottom from an autumn dusk, across a lawn Dev's mower is cutting, into a winter drift, out onto fresh snow, and back to pine as the grass grows in again. Each section is a full-bleed seasonal ground, and the seams between grounds are alive: grass blades, snow drifts and falling leaves drawn on canvas, pushed by the pointer or a finger, always in the colors of the ground they lead into. In the hero the visitor can take over a push mower and cut the lawn themselves. There are no photos, no icon cards, no quote form. The world carries the identity; the type and the button stay plain and loud. The copy speaks in Dev's own first person ("Text me", "I'll tell you a fair price").

Density is low and thumb-sized. Heavy uppercase headlines (up to 96px) sit over a quiet 17px body, and every primary interactive thing is 58px tall because the visitor is on a phone with a job in mind. One color does the work of "act here": work-glove orange, which fills the single text button, colors the header phone icon, fills the hover state of every job row, and marks the brand accent in the wordmark and the headline's second line. Focus is deliberately not orange: it is a clear blue ring so a focused button never reads as its own fill.

The build is phone-first in its CSS: base rules describe the phone, and wider layouts are added with `min-width` queries only.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed seasonal bands in fixed order: pine/dusk hero, sage services, slate winter, snow-white steps, pine close, pine-deep footer.
A living canvas edge between bands whose front layer is the next band's color, so sections grow into each other instead of meeting at a line.
A push mower in the hero lawn that mows on its own until touched, then follows the finger or mouse; cut grass regrows.
Heavy uppercase sans for headings; plain sans for reading; copy in Dev's first-person voice.
Work-glove orange is the single action color and the single brand accent; focus is blue.

One action per spot: a single orange "Text for a free estimate" pill in the hero and the close; every service is a whole-row text link with a pre-filled SMS. The phone number lives only in the header and the footer.

rules.name: The One Glove Rule
rules.body: Work-glove orange is reserved for actions (the text button, the header phone icon, row hover, selection) and the brand accent (wordmark "Dev", the headline's second line, the favicon "D"). It is never a section ground, a decorative fill, body text, or the focus ring. In the canvas world the one orange object is Dev's own push mower deck: his equipment wears the glove color because it is the thing the visitor's hand takes over. The autumn leaf colors are world material in their own hues, not the UI accent, and are never used in CSS.

rules.name: The Blue Focus Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is a 3px blue outline with a 3px offset and 6px corner, sky blue on dark grounds and deep blue on sage and snow. Never orange, so focus never merges with the button fill.

rules.name: The No-Black Rule
rules.body: No ground is black or near-neutral dark. The darkest surface is pine deep; shadows and text halos are pine- or slate-tinted, never pure black.

rules.name: The Band Text Rule
rules.body: Each ground has a fixed text pair: paper / paper soft on pine, paper / frost soft on slate, yard ink / yard ink soft on sage and snow. Do not mix pairs across grounds.

rules.name: The System-Stack Rule
rules.body: The platform sans stack is the brand voice, by Ellie's house style for these sites (pitch-site ellie-taste.md, Type: "the system font stack, heavy uppercase display headings ... It's fast and it worked"). It is a deliberate owner choice that overrides Impeccable's craft-floor preference for a sourced display face: no web fonts, no font downloads, nothing to slow the first screen on cellular.

rules.name: The 96 Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No type exceeds 96px. Display sizes scale with viewport width and stop at 96.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-Heading Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to h1-h3 and the wordmark only. Body, labels, buttons and rows stay sentence case.

rules.name: The 16px Floor Rule
rules.body: Reading text on the page never goes below 16px. The pitch line is fitted to one line between 20px and 16px by script, then wraps rather than shrink further (its 14px CSS floor is only a pre-script fallback). The `mock-ui` sizes (15px, 13px) live only inside the desktop message preview, which imitates a phone screen.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Every tap target is at least 44px; the text button and job rows are 58px, the Facebook pill 48px. On phones the text button runs full-width.

rules.name: The Lawn-Is-A-Surface Rule
rules.body: Over the hero's lawn band a transparent mow zone (96px phone, 120px wider) takes `touch-action: none`, so a drag in any direction mows instead of scrolling; the page sets `overscroll-behavior-y: none` so mowing never rubber-bands the page. Keep the zone to the lawn band only, never over copy or the button.

rules.name: The Lift-What-You-Tap Rule
rules.body: Box shadows go on the primary action and the message card. Lists, sections and text blocks are flat.

rules.name: The Halo-Is-Ground Rule
rules.body: Text over a living canvas carries a halo in exactly its band's ground color, never a tint, a contrasting glow, or black. It exists for legibility over particles, not as decoration.

dos: Do write base CSS for the phone and add wider layouts with `min-width` queries only.
Do keep work-glove orange for actions and the brand accent; put glove ink on top of it.
Do use the blue focus ring: `focus` on dark grounds, `focus-light` on sage and snow.
Do keep every ground in the pine, dusk, sage, slate, snow family; darkest is pine deep.
Do join bands with a `Field` edge whose front layer is the next band's color.
Do make the whole service row the link, ending in the arrow-in-circle, with a pre-filled `sms:` body naming the job.
Do give each action spot one orange text pill and keep the phone number to the header and footer.
Do halo text over a living canvas in its own ground color.
Do write copy in Dev's first person.
Do gate hover motion behind `(hover: hover)` and give every canvas a reduced-motion still frame.
Do cap display type at 96px and keep headings uppercase 900.
donts: Don't use black or neutral-gray grounds, or pure-black shadows.
Don't use orange as a section ground, decoration, focus ring, or text color outside the brand accent; the mower deck is the only orange in the canvas.
Don't put a second pill or a Call button beside the text button.
Don't put small uppercase kicker or eyebrow labels above headings.

Don't add thin decorative highlight lines (glossy top-edge strokes, accent rules under headings, gradient hairlines). The only 1px lines are the structural list and section dividers tinted from the band's own text color.
Don't add a contact form, icon-card grids, or stock photography; the text link and the living field carry the page.
